title: Ship loopbreaker as a first-class Herdr plugin
description: Expose the delivery-gate visualizer to the agent herd as a Herdr first-class citizen. Repairs LB-20-PLN-001 by enforcing the two outcomes the shape's success signal promises (tailnet-reachable route and the in-Herdr substrate pane), and LB-20-PLN-002 by making the supervision and no-stray proofs exclude their failure modes.

behaviors.title: Herdr recognizes loopbreaker as a linked plugin
behaviors.trigger: An operator runs `herdr plugin link` against the loopbreaker checkout
behaviors.expected: The plugin registers with id herdr.loopbreaker and its actions appear in the live plugin registry
behaviors.verify: Link the checkout and read back herdr.loopbreaker with its start/stop/url actions from `herdr plugin list`

behaviors.title: The systemd unit owns the serving process across a Herdr restart
behaviors.trigger: The plugin's start action runs on a host with systemd --user, and Herdr is subsequently restarted
behaviors.expected: The visualizer answers on the configured port and the systemd --user unit is active and owns the process actually bound to that port, both before and after the Herdr restart
behaviors.verify: Invoke start, assert the unit is active and its MainPID owns the listening socket on the configured port, restart Herdr, then assert unit-active and the same MainPID-owns-listener relationship again

behaviors.title: The service serves one configured database and creates no stray database
behaviors.trigger: The service starts with LOOPBREAKER_DB set in the plugin .env
behaviors.expected: The visualizer reads exactly that database, and no checkout-local .loopbreaker database is created by startup
behaviors.verify: Snapshot the checkout filesystem before start, start with a chosen LOOPBREAKER_DB, diff served issues against that database, and assert by before/after filesystem comparison that no checkout-local .loopbreaker path was created

behaviors.title: The substrate pane renders inside a Herdr popup
behaviors.trigger: An operator invokes the substrate pane action
behaviors.expected: A Herdr popup pane shows the active issue's prime block, or the all-issues dashboard when no active issue is linked
behaviors.verify: Open the pane through the real Herdr pane surface with and without a linked active issue against a disposable database, and read back the expected readout from the pane in each case

behaviors.title: The visualizer is reachable from the herd over the tailnet
behaviors.trigger: The start action completes on a host with Tailscale available
behaviors.expected: The exact tailnet URL the url action reports serves the visualizer, routing to the configured loopback port
behaviors.verify: Resolve the tailnet URL from the url action, fetch the visualizer and its /api/issues route through that URL from the tailnet, and assert the response matches the locally served instance

planning.outcome: Loopbreaker is installable and supervisable as a Herdr plugin, serving its live visualizer to the herd over the tailnet and inside a Herdr pane.
planning.appetite: One plugin-manifest plus supervised-launcher slice reusing the existing web/ visualizer.
non_goals: Building a delivery view inside the Collie PWA
Any change to Herdr core or the Collie repo
Authentication on the served visualizer beyond tailnet membership

work_units.title: Author herdr-plugin.toml with actions, build, and a substrate pane
work_units.done_when: herdr plugin link registers the plugin and its actions and pane are invokable and render the expected readout

work_units.title: Author loopbreaker-ctl.sh + systemd unit modeled on Collie
work_units.done_when: The unit owns the serving process across a Herdr restart and startup creates no stray checkout-local database

work_units.title: Publish the visualizer to the tailnet and clean the mapping up on uninstall
work_units.done_when: The reported tailnet URL serves the visualizer and uninstall removes exactly that mapping

proofs.method: Run `herdr plugin link` and read back herdr.loopbreaker with its actions from the live registry.
Assert unit-active and MainPID-owns-listener before and after a Herdr restart, not merely that the port answers.
Before/after filesystem snapshot proving no stray .loopbreaker was created, plus a served-issues diff against the chosen database.
Open the pane through the real Herdr pane surface in both linked and unlinked states and read back the expected readout.
Fetch the visualizer and /api/issues through the reported tailnet URL from the tailnet and compare against the local instance.

planning.production_wiring: herdr-plugin.toml at repo root declaring build, actions, and the substrate pane. scripts/loopbreaker-ctl.sh writes ~/.config/systemd/user/loopbreaker.service with ExecStart=node dist/cli.js serve --port PORT and Environment=LOOPBREAKER_DB, then runs systemctl --user enable --now. Herd reachability uses `tailscale serve --bg PORT` for https:443 by default, or `tailscale serve --bg --http=PORT PORT` when LOOPBREAKER_SERVE_MODE=http (Headscale/.internal); the url action resolves the tailnet name from `tailscale status --json` Self.DNSName. Uninstall removes exactly this mapping via `tailscale serve --https=443 off` or `--http=PORT off`, never a blanket `tailscale serve reset`.
planning.rollback: The uninstall action stops and disables the service, removes the systemd --user unit, and removes only loopbreaker's own tailscale serve mapping, leaving unrelated mappings, the checkout, and the .env intact. Herdr returns to exactly its prior state.
planning.migration: No stored-data migration; the service reads an existing loopbreaker database and creates none.

risks.risk: Host-global service vs loopbreaker's per-repo databases.
risks.mitigation: Serve one explicit LOOPBREAKER_DB, proven by LB-20-B3; multi-DB is a named non-goal pressured by LB-23.

risks.risk: A blanket tailscale serve reset would wipe unrelated mappings such as Collie's.
risks.mitigation: Uninstall targets only loopbreaker's own mapping, keyed off the same serve mode that created it.

risks.risk: Publishing the visualizer to the tailnet widens its exposure beyond loopback.
risks.mitigation: Exposure is bounded to tailnet members; LOOPBREAKER_SKIP_SERVE=1 keeps it loopback-only.
